summary: The sole occurrence was checked against the complete verse and is already the entry's example; no new sense, box, idiom or quotation is proposed.

ʕayni is the feminine grammatical subject, with naḏ̣iro agreement; the person who sees is represented as its possessor. The seen son is introduced by ʕal-, not a verbal patient suffix or an l-marked experiencer.

Negation and heš describe the absence of seeing up to the reference point. Keep Preterit Intransitive from the observed form; the German tense does not justify a new box. The inherited Arabic etymology is retained without new contact claims.
Does ʕal- belong to the general government of nḏ̣r, or specifically to the eye-subject construction? One already quoted clause cannot establish the full paradigm.
